samples.text: Pending a permanent fix, the period is being run on a manual basis, recorded as "Manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period". An engineer on the data platform team wrote the corrected agency code translation by hand, checked it against the current cloud code set, and released the valuation run on that basis. The override exists because the defect is now understood. The confirmed cause is "Stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register", so a corrected entry applied at the point of translation was enough to let the period complete. This position is provisional. It holds for the current period only, and the platform team will review it again before any further run reads the reference data. People deciding whether to wait can work from the following. The override is sound for this period because it corrects the exact row that the confirmed cause identifies, and it does not depend on any assumption still under test. It does not protect later periods.

The inventory valuation service failed because of one confirmed defect, recorded as "Stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register". A single row in that register translated a legacy agency code into the wrong cloud code, and the valuation job read the wrong code for every record that depended on it. That was not the first explanation on the bridge. Triage initially recorded the cause as "Overnight ERP outage", since an upstream interruption would have left the same empty valuation window. Log review then removed that line of enquiry, with the finding "ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window". After the outage theory fell away, the team classified the root cause against the product hierarchy sync service as "control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer".
